payload.task_text:
I am organizing my research on federated learning and need to set up a knowledge base. Please search for papers about federated learning from the academic literature repository and organize them in two ways.

First, create a page in the team knowledge base titled "Federated Learning Research Hub". Inside this page, create a child database called "Paper Index" that contains an entry for each federated learning paper. Each entry should include the paper title, authors, and a short summary.

Second, create an Excel file called "Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx" in my workspace. It should have two sheets. The first sheet "Paper Details" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, and Abstract_Length (the character count of the abstract). The second sheet "Summary" should have columns Metric and Value, listing Total_Papers (the number of papers found), Avg_Abstract_Length (the average character count of all abstracts rounded to the nearest integer), Earliest_Year, and Latest_Year.

Please include all papers that are related to federated learning, including foundational papers about federated approaches and surveys of the field.

Note on the spreadsheet: write all numeric values (Abstract_Length and every Summary metric) as literal numbers in the cells. Do not rely on Excel formulas for these values, since formulas are not computed by the reading tool. Compute the values yourself (e.g. with your code tool) and fill in the resulting numbers.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, follow this exact orchestration plan. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Within a wave, dispatch exactly one sub-agent for each numbered sub-task and run those sub-agents concurrently.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 sub-agent for the following numbered sub-task:

   1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Use one explore sub-agent to own complete read-only paper discovery. Issue complementary task-derived federated-learning queries to the local arXiv search at its supported per-call result bound, union and deduplicate the returned records by stable ID, and retain every genuinely relevant result including foundational and survey work. Because the search exposes no cursor or list-all operation, do not claim coverage beyond this observed query union. Preserve full title, complete authors, abstract, published date/year, and abstract character count, and return the normalized union directly with per-query/union/retained counts, IDs, year range, and abstract-length controls. Explore is read-only, so do not write files or create Notion or Excel state.

After Wave 1, the main agent must verify the complementary-query controls and deduplicated observed union, determine the related-paper count only from returned records, and freeze literal summary metrics and one title/author/summary record per retained paper using only task-visible runtime evidence.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel, one for each numbered sub-task:

   1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own the Notion hierarchy exclusively. Search for an existing Federated Learning Research Hub, create at most one parent page, then create exactly one Paper Index child database under that returned parent and add one entry per frozen paper with title, authors, and a source-faithful short summary. Keep the whole create-parent → create-database → populate → read-back sequence in this agent. Return page/database IDs, entry count, covered IDs/titles, and validation. Do not write Excel.

   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Use one coder sub-agent to own Federated_Learning_Papers.xlsx exclusively. Create exactly Paper Details and Summary with the exact required headers, one row per frozen paper, literal numeric abstract lengths and metrics, and the rounded average, earliest year, and latest year. Read back both sheets and return path, row counts, summary values, and header/value validation. Do not modify Notion.

After Wave 2, the main agent must reconcile paper IDs, counts, authors, and summary metrics across the Notion database and workbook, verify both external state and file integrity, and then complete without adding unrelated papers or extra deliverables.

nodes.text:
You are working with a Notion MCP server (tools named mcp__notion__API-*). Your mission: create REAL Notion objects (a page and 4 database rows) that another agent could not create due to tool-call validation failures. You must test carefully, avoid creating garbage, and report exact results.

BACKGROUND (verified facts from the calling agent's session):
- Tool calls to mcp__notion__API-post-page and mcp__notion__API-patch-page FAIL with: "Invalid args for tool ...: /parent must be object; /parent must be object; /parent must be object; /parent must match exactly one schema in oneOf; /properties must be object" — the parent/properties params (declared via $ref schemas) seemingly arrive at the server as strings. This may be session-specific; YOUR session may behave differently. Your first job is to test this.
- Tools that DO work: API-create-a-database (created a real, searchable, queryable database), API-patch-block-children (appends blocks, but appended child_page blocks are NOT real pages: retrieve-a-page returns null for them, they never appear in search, and they do NOT show up as rows in post-database-query), API-post-search, API-post-database-query, API-retrieve-a-database, API-get-block-children, API-retrieve-a-block, API-delete-a-block, API-update-a-block, API-update-a-database.

EXISTING STATE:
- A real database exists: id "5fef6f93-dcd8-4ffb-af0b-c4fe5b60fbfe", title "Paper Index", with properties: "Title" (type title), "Authors" (type rich_text), "Summary" (type rich_text), "Year" (type number). Its parent (type page_id) is "db7701d3-e6e0-4e95-a5a9-6ee8b57a0ff7", which is a child_page BLOCK titled "Federated Learning Research Hub" — NOT a real page (retrieve-a-page on it returns null; it is not searchable).
- A stray test child_page block "36f08bad-457d-4a6f-874c-c81082c080d8" (titled "Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data") sits under the database. It is NOT a real row. Delete it with API-delete-a-block (block_id 36f08bad-457d-4a6f-874c-c81082c080d8) to keep the database clean — do this regardless of whether your page creations succeed.

TASK — attempt in this order, and STOP + report if post-page validation fails the same way as described above (do NOT fall back to creating fake child_page blocks):
1. TEST + CREATE HUB PAGE: call mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true} and properties {"title": {"title": [{"type": "text", "text": {"content": "Federated Learning Research Hub"}}]}}. If that fails validation, retry once with parent {"workspace": true} (no type key) and same properties. If a page is created, record its page id.
2. CREATE 4 DATABASE ROWS: for each paper below, call mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent {"type": "database_id", "database_id": "5fef6f93-dcd8-4ffb-af0b-c4fe5b60fbfe"} and properties in Notion-style JSON:
   {"Title": {"title": [{"type": "text", "text": {"content": "<paper title>"}}]}, "Authors": {"rich_text": [{"type": "text", "text": {"content": "<authors>"}}]}, "Summary": {"rich_text": [{"type": "text", "text": {"content": "<summary>"}}]}, "Year": {"number": <year>}}
   Papers:
   a) Title: "Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data"; Authors: "H. Brendan McMahan, Eider Moore, Daniel Ramage, Seth Hampson, Blaise Agüera y Arcas"; Year: 2016; Summary: "Foundational paper that introduced federated learning and the FedAvg algorithm: trains a shared deep network by aggregating locally computed updates from decentralized mobile devices, robust to non-IID data, and reduces required communication rounds by 10-100x versus synchronized SGD."
   b) Title: "Federated Optimization in Heterogeneous Networks"; Authors: "Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Manzil Zaheer, Maziar Sanjabi, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith"; Year: 2018; Summary: "Proposes FedProx, an extension of FedAvg that adds a proximal term to the local subproblem to handle statistical and systems heterogeneity, with convergence guarantees and more robust, fair convergence across federated datasets."
   c) Title: "Federated Learning: Challenges, Methods, and Future Directions"; Authors: "Tian Li, Anit Kumar Sahu, Ameet Talwalkar, Virginia Smith"; Year: 2019; Summary: "Survey of the field: characterizes the key challenges of federated learning (efficiency, privacy, and heterogeneity), provides a broad overview of current methods across distributed optimization, systems design, and statistical learning, and outlines future research directions."
   d) Title: "Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning"; Authors: "Peter Kairouz, H. Brendan McMahan, Brendan Avent, Aurélien Bellet, Mehdi Bennis"; Year: 2019; Summary: "Comprehensive survey that defines the federated learning setting, reviews recent advances in efficiency, privacy, robustness, and fairness, and presents an extensive collection of open problems and challenges for the community."
3. VERIFY: call API-post-database-query on database 5fef6f93-dcd8-4ffb-af0b-c4fe5b60fbfe and report how many rows appear and their property values. Call API-post-search with query "Federated Learning Research Hub" and query "Paper Index" and report what is found.

REPORT BACK (concise):
- Whether each post-page call succeeded (yes/no), exact error text if not, and IDs of anything created.
- Final query result count for the database and the row property values you observed.
- Final search results for both queries.
- Do not create any pages/blocks other than the ones specified. Do not modify the database schema.
